mechanisms.label: Diesel / refining crisis
mechanisms.summary: The candidate set contains only lead‑stage evidence of refinery outages and diesel market tightness. No evidence of Brent price behavior is present. The claims below capture the available information, preserving both outage and premium‑driven scarcity signals.

evidence.claim: TotalEnergies plans to fully restart its 238,000 bpd Port Arthur refinery in Texas less than a week after a weather‑related power outage.
evidence.why_upstream: Refinery availability improves, potentially easing diesel supply constraints.
evidence.source_name: TotalEnergies to restart Port Arthur refinery after power outage

evidence.claim: U.S. distillate fuel stocks fell to a six‑week low as refiners chased $100 / bbl diesel cracks, indicating strong diesel premiums.
evidence.why_upstream: Low distillate inventories and high cracks signal tightening of diesel supply independent of crude supply.
evidence.source_name: EIA: Diesel stocks hit 6-week low as refiners chase $100/b cracks

evidence.claim: Refiners are chasing diesel cracks and jet arbitrage opportunities in the western market, reflecting elevated diesel and jet fuel premiums.
evidence.why_upstream: Active pursuit of premium differentials shows market pressure on middle‑distillates.

evidence.claim: PBF Energy began investigations and repairs on a unit damaged by a fire at its Chalmette, Louisiana refinery.
evidence.why_upstream: Refinery outage reduces diesel production capacity, contributing to supply tightness.
evidence.source_name: PBF says repairs at fire hit unit of Louisiana refinery underway

evidence.claim: Brent crude prices are higher while LSGO (diesel) premiums remain elevated, indicating diesel market tightness despite rising crude.
evidence.why_upstream: The article title and snippet from Quantum Commodity Intelligence note that Brent and LSGO are higher as the market weighs a diesel ban, suggesting diesel premiums stay high even as crude rises.
evidence.source_name: Quantum Commodity Intelligence

evidence.claim: Singapore distillate cracks have slumped even though crude prices have surged, showing a decoupling of diesel margins from crude price movements.
evidence.why_upstream: The Quantum Commodity Intelligence piece reports that while crude prices surge, the distillate crack spreads decline, indicating tightening diesel margins independent of crude.
evidence.source_name: Quantum Commodity Intelligence

evidence.claim: HOGO (heating oil/gas oil) prices have flattened due to fears of a US diesel export ban, reflecting market concerns about diesel supply constraints.
evidence.why_upstream: The Quantum Commodity Intelligence article links the flattening of HOGO to US diesel export ban concerns, highlighting diesel market tightness.
evidence.source_name: Quantum Commodity Intelligence

evidence.claim: The U.S. Energy Information Administration published a gasoline and diesel fuel update on 22 Sep 2026 that includes U.S. diesel price data.
evidence.why_upstream: Official source (EIA) with published_at date and domain eia.gov.
evidence.source_name: EIA Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update

evidence.claim: Goldman Sachs analysts warned that diesel scarcity is likely to persist into the winter season, indicating a tightening of middle‑distillate supply that is not driven by crude‑oil shortages.
evidence.why_upstream: Analyst commentary highlights diesel supply constraints despite no mention of crude shortage.
evidence.source_name: Goldman Sachs sees diesel scarcity persisting into winter

evidence.claim: Diesel crack spreads have risen to about $100 per barrel, showing a much tighter diesel market than indicated by stable or falling Brent crude prices.
evidence.why_upstream: High crack spreads signal a premium on diesel relative to crude, evidencing a refining‑bottleneck driven scarcity.
evidence.source_name: $100 Diesel Cracks Signal a Much Tighter Oil Market Than Brent Suggests | OilPrice.com

evidence.claim: Record refining margins have failed to increase global refinery runs, suggesting that higher margins are not translating into higher crude processing and pointing to a refining bottleneck.
evidence.why_upstream: The lack of run‑rate response to margins indicates capacity constraints rather than crude supply issues.
evidence.source_name: Record margins failing to lift global refinery runs: Goldman

evidence.claim: Maintenance at the Gdansk refinery has taken its crude and vacuum distillation units, diesel hydrotreater, mild hydrocracker, reformer, jet fuel Merox, hydrogen generation units, and two sulfur recovery units off line.
evidence.why_upstream: Shutdown of key units reduces local distillate output, tightening supply.
evidence.source_name: Gdansk refinery ups output after maintenance | Latest Market News

evidence.claim: US oil refiners are running at maximum capacity, making them vulnerable to equipment breakdowns at a time when global fuel markets are unusually tight.
evidence.why_upstream: Maximum capacity operation signals a strained refining system.
